statements.t: We are a clinical-stage biotechnology company leveraging the power of Artificial Intelligence (“AI”) for the development of precision antibodies against hard-to-drug targets in cardiometabolic and cardiopulmonary diseases.

First, we aim to develop next-generation antibody therapeutics addressing limitations of currently approved treatments, offering options with the potential to preserve muscle mass, target fat selectively, and provide durable weight loss with improved tolerability.
Second, we are prioritizing targets with strong human genetic and clinical validation, which we believe both reduces translational risk and increases the likelihood of clinical success.

Obesity is associated with a broad range of cardiometabolic and cardiopulmonary complications, therefore, we are also evaluating selected adjacent indications where our AI Drug Discovery Platform and target biology may offer differentiated therapeutic opportunities.

We have not completed any clinical trials in humans for any therapeutic protein product candidate produced using our technology, and there is a risk that we will be unsuccessful in developing or commercializing any product candidates.

In parallel, we have accelerated the development of IBIO-610, a potentially first-in-class, long-acting antibody designed to inhibit Activin E, and anticipate commencing first-in-human clinical trials in the first half of calendar year 2027.

At the core of our AI Drug Discovery Platform is an AI-enabled epitope steering engine enabling us to precisely direct antibodies to functional hotspots on even the most challenging targets—often considered undruggable.

IBIO-610 demonstrated a terminal half-life of approximately 33.2 days in obese NHPs, and based on allometric scaling approaches, we estimated a projected human half-life of up to 100 days, which may support infrequent dosing.

We have engaged a contract research organization to support the initiation of first-in-human clinical testing and anticipate initiating first-in-human clinical trials in the first half of calendar year 2027.
We currently anticipate an IND-equivalent filing in the first half of calendar year 2027.

Leveraging the AI Drug Discovery Platform, combining soluble G protein-coupled receptor (“GPCR”) analogues with mammalian display, we have engineered agonists with tailored activity across specific amylin receptor subtypes, showcasing the ability to address complex membrane protein targets with precision.
As the third obesity program from our AstralBio collaboration, this work further demonstrates the application of our AI Drug Discovery Platform to challenging GPCR targets.
The first layer, epitope engineering, leverages the patented AI-engine to target specific regions of proteins, allowing us to engineer antibodies with high specificity and efficacy.
Our Epitope Steering technology directly addresses these limitations by guiding antibody generation toward predefined regions of a target protein.
Using AI, we design engineered epitopes - precisely modeled and optimized fragments of the target - to improve structural fidelity, solubility, and stability.
This targeted approach allows us to explore antibody sequence space more efficiently while maintaining library sizes compatible with high-throughput mammalian display screening.

As part of the collaboration, we granted an exclusive license to AstralBio of our AI-powered technology to identify and engineer four (4) targets for the treatment of obesity and cardiometabolic diseases, of which AstralBio may continue the pre-clinical development and deploy its proven drug development expertise to advance candidates to an IND application.

We have the exclusive option to license four (4) obesity and cardiometabolic targets from AstralBio and as a result, we will receive the right to develop, manufacture and commercialize those targets upon exercise.
Upon mutual consent with AstralBio, we may also expand the collaboration to include additional targets in other fields.

In parallel, we initiated a bispecific antibody program targeting myostatin/activin A to treat obesity, cardiometabolic, and cardiopulmonary disorders, leveraging our proprietary technology stack as well as the technology of IBIO-600.
We expect to complete a separation and release agreement with Dr.

Our ongoing business is primarily focused on i) development of our pipeline for which we do not expect revenue for many years, if at all, and ii) on advancing our AI-driven discovery platform to develop molecules against hard to drug targets.

Our current cash, cash equivalents and investments in debt securities of approximately $76.7 million as of September 30, 2026, is anticipated to be sufficient to support operations into the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2028.

We plan to fund our future business operations using cash on hand, through proceeds realized in connection with the commercialization of our technologies, through potential proceeds from the sale or out-licensing of assets, collaborations, and through proceeds from the sale of additional equity or other securities and exercise of outstanding warrants.
However, there can be no assurance that we will be successful in implementing these plans, many of which will take several years before we realize proceeds.
We cannot be certain that such funding will be available on favorable terms or available at all.
We will continue to monitor the value of our IP as part of our annual accounting policy for impairment of long-lived assets.

statements.t: “The data presented at EASD strengthen our conviction in IBIO-610’s potential to deliver high-quality weight loss and provide important preclinical validation as we advance toward an IND-equivalent filing by the end of 2026, with plans to initiate first-in-human studies in the first half of 2027.

We also anticipate advancing IBIO-600 in the multiple ascending dose portion of the Phase 1 trial in the first quarter of 2027 and progressing our preclinical programs that aim to address the entire spectrum of cardiometabolic disease care.
